thread:
anna: Uploaded an nsys capture for a long KB-prefetch run — seeing memcpy on stream2 that looks to hold up kernels on stream0. trace: https://artifacts/internal/trace-1965 nsight snapshot attached
mike: Can you drop the timeline snippet here? are you seeing CPU-side gaps too?
anna: put a small ASCII timeline below and attached full .nsys. Main oddity: host->device memcpy on stream2 starts during kernel_A but timeline shows kernel_B only after memcpy finishes. Also CPU worker thread shows a long blocked period during that interval.
shiv: is that memcpy from the async prefetcher or from the main batcher?
anna: prefetcher. In this run prefetch had ~28% misses, so it's doing a lot of host copies. KV hit rate ~72% overall.
eli: FYI we changed kernel-selection heuristics last week to prefer newer fused-attention which pushes larger KV block sizes. That increases copy payloads for misses. Could be related.
jonathan: screenshots? do we have stream IDs and whether memcpy was pinned async or fallback sync path?
mike: best guess initially: copies are getting serialized because they're on the default stream. If we accidentally dropped the explicit stream handle in the prefetch path, cudaMemcpyAsync binds to default stream and serializes with kernels.
anna: timeline excerpt: ```Stream 0: kernel_A [0-20ms] 
Stream 2: memcpy H2D [5-35ms] 
CPU: worker_thread sleep/wait [4-34ms] 
Stream 0: kernel_B [36-52ms]``` so kernel_B only launches after memcpy ends.
eli: that definitely looks like ordering effects. If memcpy was truly async on a non-blocking stream with pinned memory, kernel_B should have overlapped. Are copies pinned?
shiv: our allocator path sometimes falls back to pageable memory for small buffers; the prefetcher recently updated to allocate on-demand which may return non-pinned memory for some batch sizes.
mike: repro plan: 1) micro-benchmark sending concurrent kernel + memcpy on explicit non-blocking streams with pinned vs pageable; 2) run same workload under nsys; 3) confirm whether `cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(..., cudaStreamNonBlocking)` makes a difference.
anna: I prepared a minimal nsys capture and a small patch to pass the per-batch stream handle into the prefetcher instead of relying on default. PR #2484.
jonathan: will review PR. also suggest adding an assert in tests to ensure `is_pinned` for prefetch buffers.
perf-bot: perf note: regression detected since commit abc123 — +18% p90 on kv-prefetch heavy traces. Dashboard: https://perf.internal/redwood/regressions/abc123
eli: that regression aligns with the kernel-selection change + the allocator tweak. If prefetches are serialized the latency hit grows nonlinearly.
shiv: quick mitigation: revert allocator change to always return pinned memory for prefetch buffers; long-term fix is explicit stream/pinned allocation and better batching heuristics to reduce miss amplification.
mike: please add a CI nsys test that captures the timeline and checks for expected overlap (simple heuristic: memcpy and kernel overlap > 10% wall time). Could be flaky but useful for catching this class.
anna: landing the stream-handle patch after reviews. will produce new nsys capture and run perf benchmarks in canary. thanks for the triage :thumbsup:
mike: also add a note to rollback plan if p90 doesn't recover in canary.
jonathan: noted — I'll queue a rollback flag on the Dedicated canary if perf stays bad.
anna: I'll post follow-ups with updated traces. thanks all.
